entities.name: Epigonus of Pergamum
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Epigonus of Pergamum was the chief sculptor to the Attalid dynasty at Pergamum from approximately 320 to 300 BCE.

He created numerous iconic works, including the famous Pergamene Altar, which showcased the dynasty's wealth and power.

Epigonus's significance lies in his ability to blend classical Greek and Hellenistic styles, influencing the development of art in the ancient Mediterranean. His legacy can be seen in the works of later sculptors and artists, including the Romans and Byzantines.

The Pergamene Altar, one of Epigonus's most notable creations, stands as a testament to the artistic prowess of the Attalid dynasty. Its intricate carvings and ornate decorations demonstrate the skill and craftsmanship of Epigonus and his contemporaries.

Despite his impact on the art world, Epigonus remains a relatively unknown figure outside of scholarly circles. His story serves as a reminder of the importance of preserving and celebrating the cultural heritage of ancient civilizations.
